description: Native cybernetic replacement, biotic enhancement, secure interface, social consequence, and long-term degradation systems from pages 117-130.

entries.title: Cybernetic Replacement Framework
entries.summary: Cybernetic replacement uses five technology levels, body-part-specific credit costs, installation time and risk, performance modifiers, body-percentage multipliers, and biotic power requirements.
body: Technology ranges from Basic prosthetics to Supreme near-organic systems. Higher technology improves performance but raises cost, installation complexity, power requirements, and maintenance burden.
Body percentage determines a separate cost multiplier and minimum technology range. Replacing more than 49% of the body also invokes the full-cyberization requirement described elsewhere.

The source prints a cost formula that appears to multiply a listed body-part cost by itself, but its Elite upper-arm example uses the listed 7,500-credit cost with a multiplier of 1 and produces 7,500 credits. The wiki preserves both and marks the written formula unresolved rather than applying a squared cost.

entries.title: Biotic Enhancement and Augmentation Catalogue
entries.summary: Twelve enhancements define technology level, power demand, benefits, disadvantages, body-replacement percentage, credit range, and installation complexity.
body: Enhancements range from Basic vision and healing units to Supreme sensory, camouflage, and temporal systems. Every benefit carries limitations involving power demand, maintenance, biological strain, cognitive overload, calibration, disorientation, or overheating.
The catalogue is descriptive. Where the source states an improvement without assigning a numeric bonus, the wiki does not invent one.

entries.title: Secure Cybernetic Interfaces and Social Stigma
entries.summary: Wireless cybernetic connections are avoided because unstable AI can intercept, corrupt, or seize systems; installation and maintenance rely on isolated hardwired terminals in controlled facilities.
body: Wireless connections are treated as an extreme security risk in a world of rogue and unstable AI. Cybernetic systems therefore use direct physical cables and isolated data-interface terminals for installation, programming, diagnosis, and maintenance.

Secure facilities prioritize physical and digital isolation over convenience. Wireless functions are limited, heavily regulated, or attempted only by unusually skilled or dangerously reckless operators.

Full cyborgs face distrust because extensive modifications are perceived as vulnerable to Synthesis Commander corruption, instability, and loss of control. This produces social stigma, isolation, restricted access, difficult integration, ethical conflict, and a persistent divide between cyberization and ideas of human integrity.
The source presents both genuine technological danger and social prejudice. The wiki records both without treating discrimination as proof that every cyberized person is corrupted.

tables.title: Cybernetic Security Practices
rows: Contain data transfer within a controlled link
Favor stability over advanced network features

sourceRefs.notes: Wireless AI-corruption risks, hardwired maintenance, controlled facilities, regulations, and societal stigma surrounding full cyborgs.

entries.title: Long-Term Cybernetic Degradation
entries.summary: Fully cyberized characters roll for degradation by decade, with escalating biological, cognitive, peripheral, and systemic failure; after forty years, rolls recur every 1d6 years.
body: The degradation system models the long-term cost of extensive cyberization. The first ten years have no significant degradation. Later decades use d100 outcome bands that become increasingly severe.
After forty or more years as a cyborg, the source instructs the player to roll once every 1d6 years rather than once per decade.

A result of 01-20 at later ages can produce a dangerous equilibrium in which no further degradation occurs. Other results progress through biological rejection, cognitive decline, peripheral failure, shutdown, and fatal collapse.
Fatal results may be survivable only through immediate hospitalization in state-of-the-art facilities; the source does not define a complete recovery procedure.

tables.title: Cybernetic Degradation by Years of Cyberization
rows: Initial systems function within normal parameters
Occasional glitches and minor data corruption
Reduced cognitive function and difficulty with complex tasks
Chronic pain or loss of biological function
Inability to perform essential mental functions
Complete loss of cybernetic limbs or senses
Severe impairment of basic life functions
Complete irreversible failure and imminent death

procedure: During the first 10 years, no degradation roll is required.
At each decade from 10 through 40 years, roll d100 on the appropriate age band.
After 40 years, roll once every 1d6 years using the 40+ band.
Apply the listed biological, cognitive, peripheral, or systemic effect.
Low through Critical results require increasing maintenance, repair, and intervention.
Fatal results require immediate state-of-the-art hospitalization to avoid death or total collapse.

sourceRefs.notes: Long-term degradation by decade, d100 outcomes, severity descriptions, and recurring 1d6-year rolls after forty years.
